comment: News ticker lines, gated by progress tier. Voice: dry, specific, deadpan, one notch past reality. Never zany. The joke is always about something real. No explaining the joke, no flagged puns, no emoji, no exclamation marks. Tier gate = total generators owned (early 0+, mid 25+, late 120+, empire 400+). Prestige lines fire only after the first sale.

early: Table 4 asked if the flame-grilled burger comes flame-grilled.
A regular has ordered the same burger 400 times and still reads the menu.
The fryer is making a noise. It is a new noise.
Someone has reviewed a burger they did not order.
Staff member called in sick via the venue's own Instagram story.
Your 3pm delivery arrived at 3pm. Enjoy this. It will not happen again.
Health inspector visited. Left with a burger and no notes.
The new special sold out in nine minutes. Prep for it begins tomorrow.
A customer has asked for the burger without the burger.
Someone tapped their card on the EFTPOS machine's screen. It worked.
The tongs are in the dishwasher. Both pairs. Simultaneously.
A man has asked whether the beef is local. It is from a paddock he drove past.
Two people are arguing about the correct order of cheese and patty.
The special board says Tuesday. It is Friday.
Someone ordered a large chips and then asked for a fork.
The bin is full. It has been full for some time.
A courier is parked in the loading zone with the engine running and no order.
A regular brought their own hot sauce. Nobody said anything.
The gas bottle is fine. Everyone has checked it four times.
A five-star review with the text: fine.
Someone asked what the vegetarian option is. It is the chips.
A child has been given a pickle and is now devastated.
The music is too loud. The music has not changed in two years.
mid: A man in Rosebery has described the patty as structurally honest.
Uber Eats has suggested a promotion. The promotion is you paying for it.
The Neutral Bay POS and the Leichhardt POS disagree about lunch.
A food blogger came in unannounced and ordered exactly what everyone else orders.
Someone has asked if you cater weddings. You said yes before thinking.
A one-star review complaining the queue was too long. Kept the receipt anyway.
The weekly special has a name nobody on the floor can pronounce.
A supplier has raised prices and called it a market adjustment.
Someone at the pass has invented a burger. It is going on the board.
A staff member has quietly fixed the fryer noise. They will not explain how.
Three separate customers have asked for the recipe. Three separate answers were given.
The reel did numbers. The comments are about the person's hands, not the burger.
Rosebery outsold Leichhardt on a Tuesday and nobody wants to discuss it.
Someone has ordered forty burgers for a site with no address.
A regular has been promoted and now orders two.
Head office is you. Head office has sent an email to itself.
A delivery driver has learned everyone's name. Morale is up.
The new hire is faster than you. This is fine. This is the goal.
A council inspector measured the sign. The sign is legal by 40mm.
Someone tried to pay in cash. It took longer than it should have.
The specials board now has a waitlist.
A rival has opened across the road with a shorter menu and better lighting.
The ticket printer has printed the same docket eleven times.
late: The cattle station has unionised and their demands are reasonable.
A private equity firm has sent a friendly email. It is nine pages.
Your ghost kitchen has a five-star rating and no front door.
The patty factory has moved to 6mm. Nobody outside the building noticed.
A franchisee in Perth has changed the recipe. Legal is drafting something warm.
Someone has written a thesis on your queue management.
The brand has been spotted on a t-shirt in a country you have never traded in.
Beef futures moved 2 percent on a rumour about your order book.
A documentary crew wants to film the grill. Only the grill.
The original Leichhardt grill has been retired. It is now in a display case.
An airline has asked about a burger that survives reheating at altitude.
Your supplier now calls you before they call the abattoir.
A competitor has hired your former grill hand and copied the wrong thing.
The board asked for a five-year plan. There is always a five-year plan.
Someone has valued the goodwill at more than the buildings.
A city council has named a laneway after a burger.
The 8mm patty has become a collector's item on a resale site.
Three hundred stores. One recipe. Two people who actually know it.
An economist has cited your pricing in a paper about inflation.
A satellite photo shows the delivery fleet. It is visible.
The night trade now outsells the day trade and nobody sleeps.
A regulator has invented a category for what you do.
empire: Flame-grilled from low earth orbit. The char marks are visible from the ground.
A nation has pegged a price index to your combo deal.
The orbital grill has requested a second orbital grill.
Somebody has ordered a burger from a research base and it arrived warm.
Your logo is on a fridge in Jakarta, a taxi in Lagos, and a boat.
The cattle station is now a postcode.
A treaty mentions beef. The treaty mentions you.
Every burger on the planet is 4 percent yours and nobody voted for it.
prestige: The new owners have changed the tongs. It is already worse.
You sold up and started again the following Tuesday.
The buyers kept the name and lost the recipe within a month.
Somebody paid real money for the goodwill and they were right to.
Second time around, you know exactly which corner to cut and you don't.
